When to Use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
When NOT: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; >=1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
A11y Fallback: Dashed/dotted line styles per series (not color alone); togglable data table with timestamps and values

Best Chart: Bar Chart horizontal or vertical (alt: Grouped Bar)
When to Use: Comparing discrete categories by magnitude; ranking or ordering is the core insight; categories <= 15; always sort descending by value
When NOT: Categories > 15 (use table or search); data has time dimension (use line); showing proportions (use waffle/stacked)
Volume Threshold: <20 categories: vertical bar; 20-50: horizontal bar; >50: paginated table
A11y Fallback: Value labels always visible on each bar; provide CSV export and sort control

Best Chart: Pie Chart or Donut (alt: Stacked Bar / Waffle)
When to Use: <=5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values; label slices with %
When NOT: Categories > 5; slice differences < 5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise values; accessibility-first context
Volume Threshold: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
A11y Fallback: Pie fails WCAG for colorblind users; stacked-bar alternative + percentage data table is a mandatory fallback

Best Chart: Scatter Plot or Bubble Chart (alt: Heat Map)
When to Use: Exploring relationship between two continuous variables; identifying clusters or outliers in a dataset
When NOT: Variables are categorical (use grouped bar); fewer than 20 points (patterns are not meaningful); mobile-primary context
Volume Threshold: <500 pts: SVG; 500-5000: Canvas at 0.6-0.8 opacity; >5000: hexbin or aggregate first
A11y Fallback: Data table with correlation coefficient annotation; shape markers (circle/square/triangle) per group

When to Use: Showing intensity/density across a 2D grid; time-based patterns (activity by hour x day); numeric color legend required
When NOT: Fewer than 20 cells (use bar); user needs to read exact values; colorblind users without pattern fallback
Volume Threshold: Up to 10000 cells efficiently; beyond that aggregate; calendar heatmap: 365 cells max per SVG
A11y Fallback: Pattern overlay for colorblind users; numerical value on hover; downloadable grid table with row/column labels

When to Use: Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user
When NOT: Regions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context
Volume Threshold: <1000 regions: SVG; >=1000: Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); global maps: tile-based rendering
A11y Fallback: Text labels for major regions; sortable data table by region name and value; keyboard-navigable regions

Best Chart: Funnel Chart or Sankey (alt: Waterfall for flows)
When to Use: Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages; highlight the biggest drop
When NOT: Stages are not sequential; values do not decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 stages
Volume Threshold: 3-8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into Other
A11y Fallback: Linear list view with stage name + count + drop-off %; explicit conversion % as text per stage; keyboard traversal

When to Use: Single KPI measured against a defined target or threshold; dashboard summary context
When NOT: No target or benchmark exists; comparing multiple KPIs at once (use bullet chart grid)
Volume Threshold: Single metric per gauge; for 3+ KPIs use bullet chart grid layout
A11y Fallback: Numerical value + % of target shown as visible text beside the chart; ARIA live region for real-time updates

Best Chart: Line with Confidence Band (alt: Ribbon Chart)
When to Use: Historical data + model predictions; communicating uncertainty range to non-technical stakeholders; distinguish actual (solid) vs forecast (dashed)
When NOT: No historical baseline; prediction confidence is too low to be useful; audience is not data-literate
Volume Threshold: Historical window 30-90 days for readability; forecast horizon <= 30% of visible x-axis range
A11y Fallback: Toggle actual/forecast independently; legend labels must include line-style description (solid vs dashed)

Best Chart: Line Chart with Highlights (alt: Scatter with Alert)
When to Use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
When NOT: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
Volume Threshold: Stream at <=60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
A11y Fallback: Shape marker (not color only) for anomaly points; text alert annotation per anomaly; anomaly summary list panel

When to Use: Showing size relationships within a hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (budget breakdown)
When NOT: Hierarchy depth > 3 levels (too complex to read); user needs to compare sibling values precisely
Volume Threshold: <200 nodes: SVG; 200-1000: Canvas; >1000: paginate or pre-filter before rendering
A11y Fallback: Collapsible tree table as the primary view; treemap as supplementary visual only; label all large areas

When to Use: Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution
When NOT: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
Volume Threshold: <50 flows: SVG; >=50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into an Other node
A11y Fallback: Flow table (Source -> Target -> Value); keyboard-traversable node list with tab stops; avoid on mobile

When to Use: Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (P&L, budget variance)
When NOT: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
Volume Threshold: 4-12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single Other bar
A11y Fallback: Table with running-total column; directional arrow icons per row (not color alone); labels on every bar

When to Use: Comparing multiple entities across the same fixed set of attributes (product feature comparison)
When NOT: Axes > 8 (unreadable); values need precise comparison (use grouped bar); audience unfamiliar with radar charts
Volume Threshold: 2-3 datasets maximum per chart; 5-8 axes; beyond 8 axes switch to parallel coordinates
A11y Fallback: Grouped bar chart as a mandatory alternative for precise reading; include raw data table

When to Use: Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only
When NOT: Non-financial audience; no OHLC data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
Volume Threshold: Real-time: Canvas required; historical: paginate by time range; max 500 candles visible at once
A11y Fallback: OHLC data table with sortable columns; numeric summary panel (daily change %); fill-vs-hollow pattern for colorblind

When to Use: Mapping connections between entities; network topology or social graph exploration context
When NOT: Node count > 500 without clustering pre-applied; user needs precise connection counts; mobile context
Volume Threshold: <=100 nodes: SVG; 101-500: Canvas; >500: must apply clustering/LOD before rendering
A11y Fallback: Fundamentally inaccessible without alternative; adjacency list table (Node A -> Node B -> Weight) is mandatory

When to Use: Showing spread, median, and outliers of a dataset; comparing distributions across multiple groups
When NOT: Fewer than 20 data points per group (distribution is not meaningful); audience unfamiliar with statistical charts
Volume Threshold: Any sample size; aggregated representation so rendering is excellent at any volume
A11y Fallback: Stats summary table (min / Q1 / median / Q3 / max / mean); outlier count annotation in chart subtitle

When to Use: Dashboard with multiple KPIs side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large
When NOT: Single KPI with emphasis (use gauge); data has no defined target range; fewer than 3 KPIs
Volume Threshold: Ideal for 3-10 bullet charts in a grid; scales to any count efficiently
A11y Fallback: Numerical values always visible (not hover-only); color ranges labeled with threshold text

When to Use: Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
When NOT: More than 5 categories (use stacked bar); exact values matter over visual proportion; very tight space
Volume Threshold: 10x10 grid standard (100 cells); for >5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
A11y Fallback: Better than pie for accessibility; percentage text always visible; grid cells labeled with aria-label; provide legend

When to Use: Exploring nested proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (org spend breakdown)
When NOT: More than 3 hierarchy levels (outer rings become unreadable); precision matters over overview; mobile
Volume Threshold: <100 nodes: SVG; 100-500: Canvas; >500: filter to top N before rendering
A11y Fallback: Collapsible indented list with percentages; breadcrumb trail for current drill-down state; table alternative mandatory

Best Chart: Decomposition Tree (alt: Decision Tree / Flow Chart)
When to Use: Decomposing a metric into contributing factors; AI-assisted analysis or BI drill-down scenarios
When NOT: No clear parent-child causal relationship; audience expects a summary rather than exploration
Volume Threshold: Up to 5 levels deep; limit visible nodes to 20 per level for readability; lazy-load deeper levels
A11y Fallback: Keyboard-navigable expand/collapse tree; screen reader announces node label + value + % impact

When to Use: Scientific/engineering context where the Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D
When NOT: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard business dashboards
Volume Threshold: WebGL required; Deck.gl: up to 1M points; Three.js: LOD required beyond 50000 pts
A11y Fallback: Fundamentally inaccessible; mandatory 2D projection view + data table; never the primary chart type in product UI

Best Chart: Streaming Area Chart (alt: Ticker / Moving Gauge)
When to Use: Live monitoring dashboards; IoT/ops data updating at >=1 Hz; user needs the current value at a glance
When NOT: Update frequency < 1/min (use periodic-refresh line chart); flashing content without reduced-motion support
Volume Threshold: Canvas/WebGL required; buffer last 60-300s of data; downsample older data on scroll
A11y Fallback: Pause/resume button required; current value shown as large text KPI; prefers-reduced-motion freezes animation

Best Chart: Word Cloud with Sentiment (alt: Sentiment Arc / Radar)
When to Use: NLP output visualization; exploratory analysis of text corpus sentiment; frequency-weighted keyword overview
When NOT: Precise values matter (word size is inherently imprecise); screen-reader context; corpus < 50 items
Volume Threshold: 50-5000 terms optimal; beyond 5000 apply top-N filtering before render; avoid on mobile
A11y Fallback: Word clouds fail screen readers; sortable list view by frequency with sentiment label column is mandatory

Best Chart: Process Map / Graph (alt: DAG / Petri Net)
When to Use: Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels
When NOT: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use a diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
Volume Threshold: <30 nodes: SVG; 30-100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
A11y Fallback: Path summary table (variant -> frequency -> avg duration); top 3 bottlenecks as a text annotation panel
